crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Tax Structuring and Planning
children.blurb: Tax structuring and planning within AI accounting covers how businesses arrange entities, transactions, and financing to manage tax obligations across jurisdictions, with attention to transfer pricing, permanent establishment, and tax attributes of AI-related assets.

children.name: Transfer Pricing
children.blurb: Transfer pricing concerns the prices charged between related entities within a multinational group for goods, services, intangibles, and financing.

children.name: Research Credits from Engineering Records
children.blurb: Research credits from engineering records concern the use of technical documentation, version histories, test logs, and design notes to substantiate research and development tax credit claims.

children.name: Sales, Use and Value Added Tax
children.blurb: Sales tax, use tax, and value added tax are transaction taxes levied on goods and services, with sales tax charged at the point of sale, use tax owed on taxable purchases where sales tax was not collected, and VAT applied at each stage of production with credit for input tax.

children.name: Audit Defence and Controversy
children.blurb: Audit defence and controversy covers the work of preparing for, responding to, and resolving disputes with tax authorities over positions that involve AI systems, data, or automated decisions.

sections.body: This field covers how companies that build or use AI handle tax obligations across borders, including how they structure entities, set prices between related parties, claim research credits, collect sales or value added tax, and defend positions in audits. Artificial intelligence is now doing concrete work here, not just planning. Software reads invoices and contracts to classify transactions for indirect tax, flags cross border payments that may trigger withholding, and matches engineering time logs to qualifying research activities for credits. Some tools draft audit responses by pulling evidence from accounting systems and prior correspondence. The work is operational, focused on reducing manual review and catching missed filings.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Indirect tax calculation and filing for sales, use and value added tax is the most mature, with many tools handling rate lookups and return preparation across jurisdictions. Transfer pricing documentation is partly automated, but the economic analysis still depends on human judgment about functions, assets and risks. Research credit claims from engineering records remain difficult because the link between a developer's commit history and a qualifying research activity is often ambiguous. Audit defence tools can retrieve documents and summarize issues, but they cannot yet argue a position or predict an outcome reliably. The honest limit is that tax law changes frequently and varies by country, so any model trained on past filings can miss a new ruling or local practice. The site tracks 210 compliance and regulation pages, which shows how much source material any system must keep current.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader would start with Tax Structuring and Planning to see how AI companies choose entity locations and holding structures, then move to Transfer Pricing to understand how related party charges for data, models and compute are documented. Research Credits from Engineering Records explains the specific problem of turning developer activity into defensible credit claims. Sales, Use and Value Added Tax covers the day to day collection and remittance obligations that most AI software sales trigger. Audit Defence and Controversy is where the other four pages meet reality, showing how positions are challenged and what evidence is needed. Together they move from setting up a structure to defending it under examination.
